dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis intact on Sep 1 with 6 of 7 confirmed indicators supportive: Global M2 at $103.4T rising on a 4-week basis, real yields at 2.34% and falling (-9bps over 4 weeks), 2s10s steepening to +38bps, Fed balance sheet flat at $6.73T, stablecoin dominance declining to 11.28%, and BTC.D firm at 58.11%—above the 55% alt-rotation threshold; DXY at 99.41 remains in the neutral band and declining, while August ISM PMI (released today Sep 1) could not be reliably verified from accessible sources; constructive macro backdrop ahead of NFP Sep 4, CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) held at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag on full aggregate); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (record high, 29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY); US M2 for June 2026 was $23.16T, confirming continued monthly expansion; global M2 rose ~$0.7T over 4 weeks from ~$102.7T (late June) to $103.4T (July composite); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global aggregate not yet available (6-week reporting lag); 4-week uptrend confirmed; status supportive (4-week rising trend met); FOMC Sep 16 is the next key catalyst for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released today (Sep 1 at 10:00 AM ET) but could not be reliably verified from accessible sources this run—value held at 55.6 (July 2026 official reading, released Aug 3); S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI final for August 2026 came in at 53.2 (from flash 53.2, down from July final 53.9), the separate S&P Global survey suggesting some softening in the sector; July ISM sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; July ISM was highest since May 2022; 4-week trend (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp) remains up; status supportive (above 50 and rising through last confirmed reading); flagged as skipped this cycle—August ISM could not be sourced reliably.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.41 on September 1, 2026 (afternoon EDT, down from 99.65 on Aug 31 and from ~99.67 Aug 28 Friday close); 4-week trend down: DXY peaked near 100.8–101.0 in late July 2026 and has declined to ~99.41, a ~1.4% decline over 4 weeks, above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by Treasury buyback program, rate-cut expectations, and post-Jackson Hole easing bias ahead of FOMC Sep 16; Fed Chair Warsh hawkish remarks (late August) provided only brief support; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.41 within 97.5–100 neutral band); NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11 are next decisive inputs—a dovish macro outcome cluster accelerates DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.34% as of August 27, 2026 (most recent available; FRED blocked this run); cross-check: Aug 20 reading confirmed at 2.35% per MacroRadar, consistent with 2.34% Aug 27 FRED print; 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 28, 2026) → 2.34% (Aug 27) = −9bps, a confirmed falling trend; 10Y nominal yield ~4.72% (Aug 31); status supportive (falling trend satisfies supportive condition per rule); the headwind rule requires both rising AND above 2%—the above-2% criterion is met, but the falling trend dominates status scoring; PCE at 3.7% YoY (July 2026) maintains elevated real yields in absolute terms, but the 4-week downtrend is the operative status driver; CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16 are the next key compression catalysts.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 1 estimate: 10Y yield 4.72% (Aug 31 H.15 confirmed from Treasury market data); 2Y yield ~4.34% (Aug 28 daily confirmed from prior run; Sep 1 FRED unavailable—FRED proxy-blocked); implied spread +38bps (+0.38%); marginal compression of 1bp from +39bps on Aug 28, driven by 10Y declining 1bp (4.73%→4.72%); 4-week steepening trend intact: ~+35bps (late July 2026) → +38bps (Sep 1 estimate) = +3bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening direction intact); upcoming catalysts: NFP (Sep 4), ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) are the next curve-shaping inputs.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,730,912M (~$6.73T) for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); next H.4.1 release due September 3, 2026—no new WALCL data available this run (FRED API proxy-blocked); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (late July / early August) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within the flat threshold; minor QT-driven dip from $6.745T (Aug 19) to $6.731T (Aug 26) = −$14B reflects routine measured QT operations; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat; QT pace stable).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate held at approximately −0.0048% (prior MacroMicro aggregate observation; CoinGlass proxy-blocked this run); independent confirmation: search sources indicate BTC funding rate 'flipped negative' in late August / early September 2026, consistent with spot buyers driving price while perp longs unwind; BTC.D at 58.11% on Sep 1 (firm, above 55%); 30-day trend flat: funding near zero throughout August, occasionally dipping slightly negative; rate well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding, no long-side overextension signal). (Value held from prior run; BTC Funding Rates flagged as skipped this cycle—CoinGlass proxy-blocked.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko Sep 1, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.71T; stablecoin dominance 11.28% (updated from 11.29% Aug 31); USD stablecoin subset ~$298B (−0.2% in 24h); BTC.D 58.11% (firm, rising from 57.96% Aug 31—above 55% alt-rotation trigger threshold; Bitcoin market cap ~$1.57T); 30-day trend down: confirmed—from ~13–14% in late July 2026 to 11.28% today; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rises—does not apply as total crypto cap is broadly flat); BTC.D holding above 55% keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs; a second weak reading reinforces the July NFP shock (−23K) and bolsters the rate-cut case heading into FOMC Sep 16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative and likely support 2Y yields and the dollar.

upcoming.title: Fed Beige Book (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Beige Book released at 2:00 PM ET, two weeks ahead of the FOMC meeting on September 16—qualitative snapshot of regional economic conditions across all 12 Fed districts; labor market health, inflation pressures, and credit conditions will be scrutinised for signals on the pace of easing; a broadly cooling Beige Book reinforces the dovish case for rate cuts, while stubborn price or wage pressures could temper cut expectations into the September FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); July ISM Services was broadly expansionary; a post-Jackson Hole services expansion above 55 reinforces the soft-landing narrative; a sub-50 reading alongside weak manufacturing data would materially shift FOMC odds toward a 50bps cut on Sep 16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read released alongside ISM Services PMI; provides early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for an aggressive cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a 50bps rate cut and likely push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; also includes unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, and labor force participation rate.
